english: I've started preparing for the job hunt.
grammar: 취업 (chwieop) = getting a job; 취업 준비 = job-hunt prep.

english: Job hunting is really hard these days.
I'm still a job seeker.
I want to work at a good company.
grammar: -고 싶어요 = want to: 다니고 싶어요 (danigo sipeoyo) = want to work there.

english: I wrote a new resume.
The cover letter is the hardest part.
grammar: 자기소개서 (jagisogaeseo) = self-intro essay, Korea's cover letter.

english: I applied to this company.
grammar: 지원하다 (jiwonhada) = to apply; 회사에 지원해요.

english: I check job postings every day.
I submitted my application yesterday.
I passed the document screening.
grammar: 붙다 (butda) = to pass a screening/exam: 시험에 붙어요.

english: Sadly, I got cut at the document stage.
grammar: 떨어지다 (tteoreojida) = to fail/be cut: 시험에 떨어졌어요.

english: I have an interview next week.
I'm preparing hard for the interview.
grammar: -고 있어요 = am -ing: 하고 있어요 (hago isseoyo) = am doing it.

english: I'm so nervous because of the interview.
grammar: 때문에 (ttaemune) = because of: 면접 때문에 = because of the interview.

english: I had my first interview today.
grammar: 첫 (cheot) = first: 첫 면접 = first interview, 첫 출근 = first day.

english: The interviewer asked a lot of questions.
I practiced likely questions in advance.
I was very nervous. Still, I answered well.
grammar: 그래도 (geuraedo) = still, even so — concedes what came before.

english: I introduced myself first.
I'm waiting for the interview results.
I finally passed the final interview.
Unfortunately I didn't make it this time.
I got a call from that company.
grammar: 연락이 오다 (yeollagi oda) = to get a call/message (lit. contact comes).

english: I start work next week.
grammar: 부터 (buteo) = from/starting: 다음 주부터 = starting next week.

english: I finally got a job.
I joined as a new employee.
Today is my first day at work. I'm so nervous.
The company atmosphere is really good.
The manager kindly explained it to me.
grammar: -아/어 주셨어요 = kindly did for me: 설명해 주셨어요 (jusyeosseoyo), honored subject.

english: The manager began the meeting.
grammar: Honored subject takes -(으)시-: 부장님이 시작하셨어요 (sijakhasyeosseoyo).

english: I work in the marketing department.
My coworkers are all kind.
grammar: 동료 (dongnyo) = coworker; -들 makes it plural: 동료들 = coworkers.

english: I'm learning my new duties.
I took on this project.
grammar: 맡다 (matda) = to take charge of: 일을 맡아요 = take on a task.

english: I'll prepare the meeting materials.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ게요 = I'll (promise): 준비할게요 (junbihalgeyo) = I'll get it ready.

english: I have to submit the report by today.
grammar: -아/어야 해요 = have to: 내야 해요 (naeya haeyo) = have to submit it.

english: There is a lot of overtime this week.
There are company dinners way too often.
I'm going on a business trip next month.
I respect my boss.
I sent an email to the manager.
grammar: To a superior use 께 not 한테: 부장님께 (bujangnimkke) = to the manager.

english: I asked the team leader.
grammar: 여쭤보다 (yeojjyeoboda) = humbly ask a superior; pairs with 께.

english: The meeting took a whole three hours.
grammar: Hours use native numbers: 세 시간 (se sigan) = three hours; -이나 = as much as.

english: My desk is by the window.
The lunch break is one hour.
I want to build up my qualifications more.
I earned one more certificate.
I need an English score.
I go to an academy even on weekends.
grammar: -에도 = even at/on: 주말에도 (jumare-do) = even on weekends.

english: I'm doing an internship this summer.
The internship experience really helped.
grammar: 도움이 되다 (doumi doeda) = to be helpful: 도움이 됐어요 = it helped.

english: I want my experience to be recognized.
I applied as an experienced hire.
grammar: 경력직 (gyeongnyeokjik) = experienced-hire position (vs 신입 = new hire).

english: I want to become a permanent employee.
For now I work on a contract.
The company hired me as a permanent employee.
The probation period is three months.
grammar: 수습 기간 (suseup gigan) = probation period for a new hire.

english: I received the work handover.
I'm so happy to have gotten my first paycheck.
grammar: -아/어서 = and so: 받아서 (badaseo) = got it, and so...

english: I bought my parents their first gift from me.
grammar: -아/어 드리다 = do humbly for an elder: 사 드렸어요 (sa deuryeosseoyo).

english: My company has good benefits.
I'm going to use my annual leave next week.
grammar: 연차 (yeoncha) = paid annual leave; 연차를 쓰다 = take leave.

english: I got a bonus this month.
The performance pay was more than I expected.
I finally got promoted to assistant manager.
grammar: 승진하다 (seungjinhada) = to be promoted; 대리 = a junior manager rank.

english: My annual salary went up a little.
grammar: 연봉 (yeonbong) = annual salary; 오르다 → 올랐어요 = went up.

english: I want to negotiate my salary well.
I requested a raise from the company.
My salary came into my account.
After taxes, the take-home pay is small.
grammar: -(으)면 = if/when: 빼면 (ppaemyeon) = if you subtract it.

english: Work-life balance really matters these days.
There's so much overtime, it's exhausting.
grammar: -아/어서 = because: 많아서 (manaseo) = because there's a lot.

english: So I'm thinking about changing jobs.
I want to move to better conditions.
I put in a resume at another company.
I'll change jobs using my experience.
grammar: 살리다 → 살려서 (sallyeoseo) = making use of it; -(으)ㄹ 거예요 = will.

english: I've decided to resign next month.
grammar: -기로 했어요 = decided to: 퇴사하기로 했어요 (toesahagiro haesseoyo).

english: I handed in my resignation yesterday.
The manager was quite sorry to see me go.
grammar: Others feelings take -어하다: 부장님이 아쉬워하셨어요 (aswiwohasyeosseoyo).

english: My coworkers threw me a farewell party.
Next week is my last working day.
I want to settle in well at the new workplace.
I want to make a good impression in the interview.
It takes a whole hour to get to the office.
grammar: -까지 = up to/as far as: 회사까지 (hoesakkaji) = all the way to the office.

english: There are days I work from home too.
My dream is to get into a big company.
I actually prefer a small company.
I prepared my interview outfit in advance.
My hands shook and I spilled the coffee.
The interview's over, so I feel at ease.
I told my parents the news that I passed.
My parents were really pleased.
grammar: Others feelings use 좋아하다 not 좋다: 좋아하셨어요 (joahasyeosseoyo) = were pleased.

english: I spoke confidently in the interview.
grammar: 자신 있게 (jasin itge) = confidently; -게 turns an adjective into an adverb.

english: I work diligently.
This job suits me well.
The new team leader is really nice.
grammar: Honored subject: 좋으세요 (joeuseyo) adds -(으)세요 to describe 팀장님.

english: A senior colleague taught me a lot.
A junior colleague has already joined.
You must follow the company rules.
I really love this profession.
My goal is to become a team leader.
grammar: -는 거예요 = it is (doing): 되는 거예요 (doeneun geoyeyo) = is to become.

english: If you work hard, opportunities come.
It's okay even if you make a mistake.
grammar: -아/어도 괜찮아요 = it's okay even if: 실수해도 (silsuhaedo).

english: Next time I'll definitely pass.
grammar: 붙다 → 붙을 거예요 (buteul geoyeyo) = will pass; 꼭 = for sure.

english: I didn't give up and kept applying.
grammar: -지 않고 = without doing: 포기하지 않고 (pogihaji anko) = without giving up.

english: This time I feel confident.
The office is close to home, which is nice.
grammar: 가깝다 → 가까워서 (gakkawoseo) = because it's near.

english: I start work at nine in the morning.
grammar: Clock hours use native numbers: 아홉 시 (ahop si) = nine o'clock.

english: I usually leave work at six.
I took a half-day off today.
I'm moving to a different department next month.
grammar: 옮기다 → 옮겨요 (omgyeoyo) = move/transfer (something).

english: It is new work. So I am a little nervous.
grammar: 새롭다 → 새로운 (saeroun) = new, before a noun: 새로운 일 = new work.

english: A coworker helped, so I got used to it fast.
On Mondays there are so many meetings.
This project wrapped up well.
The manager praised me a lot.
grammar: 칭찬하다 (chingchanhada) = to praise; honored subject → 칭찬하셨어요.

english: There's a workshop next week.
I had new business cards made.
I got a company email address.
I want to work in this field.
I'm a little worried because I lack experience.
Still, I just need to learn hard.
grammar: -(으)면 돼요 = it's enough if / just need to: 배우면 돼요 (baeumyeon dwaeyo).

english: I like working with people.
grammar: -는 게 좋아요 = like doing: 일하는 게 (ilhaneun ge) = the working (of it).

english: I want to get promoted next year.
I'm building my career step by step.
I opened an account at the bank.
grammar: 계좌 (gyejwa) = bank account; 계좌를 만들다 = to open an account.

english: I opened a new bank account.
I want to open one more account.
grammar: Counters use native numbers: 하나 (hana) = one; 하나 더 = one more.

english: There's hardly any balance in my account.
grammar: 잔액 (janaek) = balance; 얼마 없다 = there's barely any left.

english: I made a separate salary account.
I updated my bankbook after a long time.
I waited at the bank counter.
I take a number and wait.
grammar: 번호표 (beonhopyo) = queue ticket; 뽑다 → 뽑고 = take one and...

english: I forgot my account PIN.
You have to bring your ID.
grammar: -아/어야 해요 = have to: 가져가야 해요 (gajyeogaya haeyo) = must take it.

english: I signed up for internet banking.
I check my balance on the app.
grammar: -(으)로 = by means of: 앱으로 (aebeuro) = via the app.

english: I put money into my account.
I withdrew a little cash.
The bank closes at four.
grammar: Clock hours use native numbers: 네 시 (ne si) = four o'clock.

english: I pay into a savings plan every month.
I signed up for a three-year savings plan.
grammar: -짜리 = one worth/of: 삼 년짜리 (sam nyeonjjari) = a three-year one.

english: I save 500,000 won each month.
grammar: Money uses Sino numbers: 오십만 원 (osimman won) = 500,000 won.

english: I want to build up a lump sum.
The deposit interest is too low.
The interest rate is 2 percent.
grammar: 퍼센트 (peosenteu) uses Sino numbers: 이 퍼센트 = two percent.

english: A saving habit is important.
I'm saving an emergency fund separately.
I save money little by little.
My savings plan matures next month.
When it matures, I'll have a lump sum.
grammar: -(으)면 = when: 되면 (doemyeon) = when it becomes/matures.

english: I'll travel with that money.
grammar: -(으)로 = with/using: 그 돈으로 (geu doneuro) = with that money.

english: I save diligently.
Looking at my bankbook, I feel proud.
grammar: 뿌듯하다 (ppudeuthada) = to feel proud/fulfilled (first person).

english: I set a target amount.
I got a new credit card.
I only use a debit card.
My card bill came out high this month.
grammar: 카드값 (kadeukap) = card bill; 나오다 → 나왔어요 = came out.

english: I paid in installments.
I bought it in three monthly installments.
grammar: 개월 uses Sino numbers: 삼 개월 (sam gaewol) = three months.

english: I paid all at once.
I swiped my card way too much.
grammar: 긁다 → 긁었어요 (geulgeosseoyo) = swiped (a card), slang for overspending.

english: Next month I'll cut back on the card.
grammar: 줄이다 → 줄일 거예요 (juril geoyeyo) = will reduce it.

english: I've racked up a lot of card points.
grammar: 쌓이다 → 쌓였어요 (ssayeosseoyo) = piled up, accumulated.

english: I lost my card, so I reported it right away.
My card limit is maxed out.
grammar: 한도 (hando) = limit; 차다 → 찼어요 = got full/reached.

english: I find cards more convenient than cash.
grammar: -보다 = than: 현금보다 (hyeongeumboda) = than cash.

english: I checked my card statement.
I transferred money to a friend.
I sent it straight to the account.
A transfer fee was added.
grammar: 수수료 (susuryo) = fee/commission; 붙다 → 붙었어요 = got attached.

english: I pay the rent by bank transfer.
It goes out by auto-transfer every month.
grammar: 자동이체 (jadong-iche) = automatic transfer/direct debit.

english: I sent money to the wrong account.
grammar: 잘못된 (jalmotdoen) = wrong/mistaken (before a noun).

english: I called the bank and cancelled it.
grammar: -아/어서 = and then: 전화해서 (jeonhwahaeseo) = called, and then...

english: I deposited money into the account.
I withdrew money from the ATM.
There's a set withdrawal limit.
grammar: 출금 (chulgeum) = withdrawal; -아/어 있어요 = is (in a state).

english: A lot of money went out this month.
grammar: 나가다 → 나갔어요 (nagasseoyo) = went out/was spent.

english: I put loose change in the piggy bank.
I exchanged currency at the bank.
I changed it to dollars before the trip.
I took out a loan at the bank.
I'm still paying off my student loan.
The loan interest is such a burden.
grammar: 부담스럽다 → 부담스러워요 (budamseureowoyo) = feels burdensome (ㅂ-irr).

english: I have to pay interest every month.
grammar: 이자를 내다 (ijareul naeda) = to pay interest; -아/어야 해요 = have to.

english: I want to pay off the loan fast.
I paid off a bit of the principal this month.
Interest rates went up again.
I borrowed money from a friend.
I'll definitely pay it back next month.
grammar: -(으)ㄹ게요 = I promise to: 갚을게요 (gapeulgeyo) = I'll pay it back.

english: I have no debt, so I feel at ease.
grammar: 빚 (bit) = debt; 빚이 없다 = to be debt-free.

english: If you take a loan, interest builds up.
grammar: -(으)면 = if: 받으면 (badeumyeon) = if you take/receive it.

english: I manage my credit score well.
I'm looking for a bank with low interest.
grammar: 낮은 (najeun) = low (before a noun): 이자가 낮은 은행.

english: I got a loan consultation.
I pay taxes every year.
The property tax bill came this month.
Income tax is more than I thought.
I'm getting ready for year-end tax settlement.
I got a small tax refund.
Tax is deducted from my salary.
grammar: 빠지다 → 빠져요 (ppajyeoyo) = to be taken out/deducted; 에서 = from.

english: I filed my taxes within the deadline.
VAT is 10 percent.
Because of taxes, take-home pay shrinks.
grammar: 줄다 → 줄어요 (jureoyo) = to decrease; 실수령액 = take-home amount.

english: Tax calculations are so complicated.
I keep a household ledger every day.
I tallied up this month's spending.
My spending is more than my income.
grammar: 수입 (suip) = income; -보다 더 = more than: 수입보다 더 많아요.

english: Living costs are high.
grammar: 생활비 (saenghwalbi) = living expenses; (돈이) 들다 = to cost.

english: I made a budget for this month.
I mustn't go over budget.
grammar: -(으)면 안 돼요 = must not: 넘으면 안 돼요 (neomeumyeon an dwaeyo).

english: I need to cut down on eating out.
grammar: 줄이다 → 줄여야 해요 (juryeoya haeyo) = have to reduce; 외식비 = dining-out cost.

english: I even save on coffee.
I often regret impulse buys.
I try to buy only what I need.
grammar: -(으)려고 해요 = intend to: 사려고 해요 (saryeogo haeyo) = plan to buy.

english: I give my kid an allowance every week.
grammar: 용돈 (yongdon) = pocket money/allowance; 매주 = every week.

english: The kids' education costs are really high.
I paid the utility bills on time.
The electricity bill is higher than last month.
I saved a lot of money this month.
I want to manage money well.
My husband and I keep the ledger together.
grammar: -(이)랑 = with: 남편이랑 (nampyeon-irang) = with my husband.

english: Saving has become a habit now.
grammar: 절약 (jeollyak) = thrift/saving; -이 되다 → 됐어요 = became.

target: 제 목표는 빚을 다 갚는 거예요.
english: My goal is to pay off all my debt.
grammar: -는 거예요 = is (to do): 갚는 거예요 (gapneun geoyeyo) = is to pay off.

english: I'm very interested in personal finance.
These days I'm investing in stocks.
I invest a little at a time in small amounts.
I'm happy my stocks went up a bit.
grammar: 오르다 → 올라서 (ollaseo) = because it rose (first-person 기뻐요).

english: I signed up for a fund too.
Investing always carries risk.
I don't make reckless investments.
grammar: 무리한 (murihan) = excessive/overreaching (before a noun).

english: I'm preparing for retirement from now.
I pay into a pension every month.
I've gotten interested in real estate too.
Housing prices have risen a lot lately.
grammar: 집값 (jipgap) = house price; 오르다 → 올랐어요 = rose.

english: I started studying personal finance.
I got advice from an expert.
I want to spend money wisely.
grammar: 현명하게 (hyeonmyeonghage) = wisely; -게 makes an adverb.

english: I want to slowly become well-off.
The exchange rate rose, so travel feels pricey.
I exchanged money at the airport.
I carry only a little cash around.
These days I pay almost everything by mobile.
I lost my wallet, so I remade my card.
grammar: 잃어버리다 → 잃어버려서 (ireobeoryeoseo) = lost it, and so...

english: The bank app is really convenient.
I've come to enjoy saving.
I spend money according to a plan.
grammar: 계획적으로 (gyehoekjeogeuro) = in a planned way, methodically.

english: I prepare retirement funds in advance.
Health matters more than money.
grammar: -보다 더 = more than: 돈보다 (donboda) = more than money.
